title: THE FIRST FRAME
goal: Catch the thought before it becomes the room.
steps:
1. Trigger — A trigger flickers.
2. Pause Story — Do not explain it yet.
3. Capture Thought — Pin the first thought, picture, or prediction exactly as it arrived.
4. Quote — Put quotation marks around it.
5. Close Capture — The catch ends there; no life story, no courtroom, no spiral.
win: ✓ One thought stayed one thought; the courtroom never opened.
supports:
• Exhale after “Close Capture”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Capture Thought”.
• “Quote” — the rule loosened.
• “Trigger” versus “Close Capture”: what eased?
• I can use “Pause Story” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Trigger → Pause Story → Capture Thought → Quote → Close Capture

title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.
win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
supports:
• Exhale after “Balance Verdict”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Sort Facts” on return.
• “Switch Sides” separates feeling from fact.
• “Imagine Trays” → “Balance Verdict”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Sides” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict

title: THE GREY DIAL
goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.
steps:
1. Name Extremes — Name the two extremes your mind is using.
2. Build Scale — Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
3. Place Today — Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts.
4. Choose Response — Choose a response matched to that exact setting.
win: ✓ The dial found a middle, and the response found its size.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Response”; keep both sides.
• Restart detected: “Place Today”.
• “Place Today” widens the evidence field.
• “Name Extremes” versus “Choose Response”: what eased?
• I can use “Build Scale” before concluding.

title: THE RULE UNDER THE RULE
goal: A surface thought often works for a hidden constitution.
steps:
1. Picture Painful — Picture the painful thought.
2. Ask Meaning — Ask, ‘If that were true, what would it mean about me, others, or life?’ Answer quickly, then ask the same question of the answer.
3. Continue Stable — Continue only until one stable rule repeats.
4. Box Rule — Put that rule in a mental box.
5. Apply Today — Today’s task is to inspect it, not obey it.

• Loop back? Use “Continue Stable”.
• “Box Rule” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Picture Painful” → “Apply Today”?
• I can use “Ask Meaning” without perfecting.

TITLE
THE FORECAST SCOREBOARD

GOAL
Memory edits its predictions after the result.

RITUAL
1. Count Hit — Before an uncertain event, remember four items: prediction, confidence %, deadline, and what counts as a hit.
2. Keep Result — Afterward, hold the result without rewriting the original entry.
3. Calculate — Calculate the gap between confidence and reality.
4. Spot the Bias — After five rounds, look for your recurring bias.

WIN
✓ Forecast bias exposed. Memory cannot quietly rewrite the scoreboard now.

• Exhale after “Spot the Bias”; release the score.
• Return once to “Calculate”.
• “Calculate” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Count Hit” → “Spot the Bias”?
• I can use “Keep Result” without perfecting.

Count Hit → Keep Result → Calculate → Spot the Bias

title: TRANSLATE THE VERDICT
goal: ‘Bad’ is compressed data. Decompress it.
steps:
1. Take Judgement — Take one judgement and mentally translate it into three components: visible facts, personal preference, likely consequence.
2. Prefer Decision — Example: ‘Awful meeting’ becomes ‘Two interruptions; I prefer turn-taking; the decision stayed unclear.’ Respond to the components rather than fighting the label.
win: ✓ I unpacked the verdict into facts I could actually respond to.
supports:
• Exhale after “Prefer Decision”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Prefer Decision”.
• “Take Judgement” — fear isn’t fate.
• Difference check: “Take Judgement” → “Prefer Decision”.
• I can use “Prefer Decision” while fear stays loud.

title: REVERSE THE URGE, COMPLETELY
goal: When the emotion is unjustified, half-opposites do not retrain it.
steps:
1. Check Support — Verify that the facts do not support the action impulse.
2. Speak Gently — Then do its full safe opposite: approach instead of avoid, speak gently instead of attack, straighten instead of collapse, engage instead of hide.
3. Match Posture — Match posture, words, and behaviour until the new signal is coherent.
win: ✓ Desire got a seat, not the steering wheel.
supports:
• Exhale after “Match Posture”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Speak Gently”.
• “Speak Gently” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Check Support” → “Match Posture”?
• I can use “Speak Gently” without obeying the urge.

title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.
steps:

Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.

RITUAL
1. Identify Chapter — Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling.
2. Permit — Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
3. Pause Meaning — If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet.
4. Continue Genuine — Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears.

WIN
✓ One emotional chapter reached a real ending marker.

• Exhale after “Continue Genuine”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Pause Meaning”.
• “Pause Meaning” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Continue Genuine”: what changed from “Identify Chapter”?
• I can use “Permit” without obeying the urge.

FORMULA FLOW
Identify Chapter → Permit → Pause Meaning → Continue Genuine

PAUSE
Stop if the process floods awareness or removes action control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAMP WHERE THE DETAIL CAME FROM
goal: A memory matters without every detail carrying equal certainty.
steps:
1. Pick Detail — Choose one small memory detail; do not replay the event.
2. Tag Source — Stamp it SENSED, INFERRED, LEARNED LATER, or UNSURE.
3. Rate Confidence — Give the detail a confidence word—high, medium, low, or unknown—based on its source rather than its emotional intensity.
4. Keep Core — Picture one core fact that remains reliable and let the other detail keep its honest uncertainty.
win: ✓ The memory kept a reliable core and honest fog around the rest.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Core”; leave it unanswered.
• Skip replay; use “Rate Confidence”.
• “Rate Confidence” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• What changed: “Pick Detail” → “Keep Core”?
• I can use “Tag Source” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Pick Detail → Tag Source → Rate Confidence → Keep Core

title: FIND THE FIRST ‘I’
goal: Sense of ‘I’ has an entrance point.
steps:
1. Experience — Notice an experience before describing it.
2. Wait Moment — Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
3. Trace Addition — Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location.
4. Observe Attachment — Observe the attachment without removing it.
5. Do the Task — The task is detection, not metaphysical victory.
win: ✓ I found the ‘I’ without needing to solve who ‘I’ ultimately am.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Do the Task”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Trace Addition”.
• “Observe Attachment” keeps sensation as data.
• Compare “Experience” with “Do the Task”.
• I can use “Wait Moment” while sensation stays.

display.full_ritual:
TITLE
FIND THE FIRST ‘I’

GOAL
Sense of ‘I’ has an entrance point.

RITUAL
1. Experience — Notice an experience before describing it.
2. Wait Moment — Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
3. Trace Addition — Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location.
4. Observe Attachment — Observe the attachment without removing it.
5. Do the Task — The task is detection, not metaphysical victory.

WIN
✓ I found the ‘I’ without needing to solve who ‘I’ ultimately am.

• Gently exhale after “Do the Task”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Trace Addition”.
• “Observe Attachment” keeps sensation as data.
• Compare “Experience” with “Do the Task”.
• I can use “Wait Moment” while sensation stays.

FORMULA FLOW
Experience → Wait Moment → Trace Addition → Observe Attachment → Do the Task

PAUSE
Stop if the search produces feeling unreal or detached from yourself or panic.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION
goal: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.
steps:
1. Move Body — Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease.
2. Ask Change — At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
3. Keep All Layers — Do not discard any layer.
4. Place Like — Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action.
win: ✓ Five layers became one usable next layer.

• Restart detected: “Keep All Layers”.
• “Keep All Layers” keeps sensation as data.
• What lost power: “Move Body” → “Place Like”?
• I can use “Ask Change” while sensation stays.

title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
goal: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
steps:
1. Take Event — Take one rigid reading of an event.
2. Compare Dream — Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Identify Facts — Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
4. Try Construction — Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.
win: ✓ Another person’s response moved out of the judge’s chair.
supports:
• Exhale after “Try Construction”; drop the scoreboard.
• Return once to “Identify Facts”.
• “Identify Facts” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• At “Try Construction”, compare “Take Event”.
• I can use “Compare Dream” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Take Event → Compare Dream → Identify Facts → Try Construction
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid dreamlike framing if it increases derealisation or psychotic symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THE PROJECTION TO SENDER
goal: The mind may be viewing its expectation on someone else’s screen.

title: CHANGE ONE LENS, WATCH THE WORLD
goal: Experience partly inherits the meaning that organises it.
steps:
1. Choose Event — Choose a current event and picture the lens being used.
2. Replace Plausible — Replace it with one plausible alternative—not a positive slogan.
3. Act Lens — Spend five minutes acting from the alternate lens and observe changes in body, attention, and available choices.
win: ✓ I changed one lens and watched the available choices change with it.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Act Lens”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Replace Plausible”.
• “Replace Plausible” — alarm isn’t command.
• Difference check: “Choose Event” → “Act Lens”.
• I can use “Replace Plausible” while alarm rises.

title: BOX THE PROBLEM
goal: Scattered distress cannot be solved because it has no edges.
steps:
1. Picture Lines — Picture three lines: CURRENT CONDITION; DESIRED CONDITION; MEASURABLE GAP.
2. Remove History — Remove history unless it changes the gap.
3. Give Problem — Give the problem a time horizon and one owner.
4. Statement — If the statement still contains ‘everything,’ shrink it again.
win: ✓ I boxed the problem until ‘everything’ could no longer fit inside it.
supports:
• Exhale after “Statement”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Give Problem”.
• “Give Problem” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Picture Lines” → “Statement”.
• I can use “Remove History” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Lines → Remove History → Give Problem → Statement

PAUSE

content:
TITLE
THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM

GOAL
Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.

RITUAL
1. Start Brief — Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
2. Include Conventional — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility.
3. Test Feasibility — Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room.

WIN
✓ I let options multiply before judgement was allowed into the room.

• Exhale after “Test Feasibility”; soften the jaw.
• On return: “Include Conventional”.
• “Include Conventional” keeps clarity above heat.
• What changed: “Start Brief” → “Test Feasibility”?
• I can use “Include Conventional” without extra heat.

FORMULA FLOW
Start Brief → Include Conventional → Test Feasibility

PAUSE
Exclude choices that violate ethics, consent, law, or safety from the start.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DECIDE THE STOPPING LINE FIRST
goal: Analysis cannot finish if ‘enough’ has no definition.
steps:
1. State Minimum — Before researching, state the minimum evidence required to choose: number of quotes, critical facts, confidence level, or deadline.
2. Picture Genuinely — Picture what would really reverse the decision.
3. Select Further — When the threshold is met, select; further information needs a new reason for entry.
win: ✓ Clarity survived the emotion.
supports:
• Exhale after “Select Further”; soften the jaw.
• On return: “Picture Genuinely”.
• “Picture Genuinely” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Select Further”, compare “State Minimum”.
• I can use “Picture Genuinely” without extra heat.
formula_flow: State Minimum → Picture Genuinely → Select Further

title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
goal: Residual body alarm is not fresh evidence.
steps:
1. Set Reasonable — Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, replay, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes.
2. Picture Time — Picture its end time.
3. Notice Sensations — Until then, keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened.
4. Reassess — Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible.
win: ✓ I recognised the aftershock as residue, not fresh evidence.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reassess”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Notice Sensations”.
• “Notice Sensations” proves motion is available.
• “Reassess”: what changed from “Set Reasonable”?
• I can use “Picture Time” before motivation.
formula_flow: Set Reasonable → Picture Time → Notice Sensations → Reassess

title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
goal: Analysis may keep interrupting an unfinished inner sequence.
steps:

2. Allow Move — Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
3. Check Your Position — Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes.
4. Use Sensory — Reorient afterward using present sensory facts.
win: ✓ I let the image reach its last frame instead of interrupting it with analysis.
supports:
• Exhale after “Use Sensory”; notice the room.
• Use “Check Your Position” on return.
• “Check Your Position” proves the present returned.
• Difference check: “Bring Image” → “Use Sensory”.
• I can use “Allow Move” to return here.
formula_flow: Bring Image → Allow Move → Check Your Position → Use Sensory

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
steps:
1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.
win: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.
supports:
• Exhale after “Preserve Forecast”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Name Miss”, once.
• “Name Miss” puts facts above speed.
• “Keep Both Versions” to “Preserve Forecast”: what loosened?
• I can use “State Size” without rushing.
formula_flow: Keep Both Versions → State Size → Name Miss → Preserve Forecast
safety:
PAUSE
Do not overlearn from one noisy or unrepresentative result.

title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
goal: Certainty and support need separate meters.
steps:
1. Rate Sure — Rate how sure you feel from 0–100.
2. Rate Evidence — Independently rate evidence quality using source reliability, directness, and recency.
3. Separate Meters — Picture the two scores on separate meters so certainty cannot masquerade as evidence.
4. Follow Evidence — Let the evidence meter choose the action; treat the confidence meter as a feeling to notice, not a vote.
win: ✓ Evidence got the vote. Confidence stayed a feeling.
supports:

• On return: “Separate Meters”.
• “Separate Meters” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “Rate Sure” → “Follow Evidence”.
• I can use “Rate Evidence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Rate Sure → Rate Evidence → Separate Meters → Follow Evidence

goal: Old evidence should not command new conditions forever.

title: SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS
goal: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.
steps:
1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the one simple action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.
win: ✓ Three premises produced three worlds; only the robust action survived all of them.
supports:
• Exhale after “Compare Action”; keep both sides.
• On return: “Identify Action”.
• “Identify Action” widens the evidence field.
• What lost power: “Keep Observations” → “Compare Action”?
• I can use “Reframe Three Ways” before concluding.

title: FORECAST WITH A LANDING ZONE
goal: Accuracy can include an honest margin of error.
steps:
1. Predict Range — Predict a range rather than a perfect point.
2. State Acceptable — State the acceptable error band and why it is reasonable.
3. Measure Reality — After the result, measure reality check: inside, near, or outside the band.
4. Widen the Landing — Adjust future range width instead of declaring success or failure.
win: ✓ The forecast became a range, so reality had somewhere honest to land.
supports:
• Exhale after “Widen the Landing”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Measure Reality”.
• “Measure Reality” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Widen the Landing”: what changed from “Predict Range”?
• I can use “State Acceptable” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Predict Range → State Acceptable → Measure Reality → Widen the Landing

Accuracy can include an honest margin of error.

RITUAL
1. Predict Range — Predict a range rather than a perfect point.
2. State Acceptable — State the acceptable error band and why it is reasonable.
3. Measure Reality — After the result, measure reality check: inside, near, or outside the band.
4. Widen the Landing — Adjust future range width instead of declaring success or failure.

WIN
✓ The forecast became a range, so reality had somewhere honest to land.

• Exhale after “Widen the Landing”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Measure Reality”.
• “Measure Reality” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Widen the Landing”: what changed from “Predict Range”?
• I can use “State Acceptable” without perfecting.

FORMULA FLOW
Predict Range → State Acceptable → Measure Reality → Widen the Landing

PAUSE
Keep tight limits where safety or engineering precision requires them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

steps:

title: KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY
goal: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.
steps:
1. Hold Trigger — Hold the trigger at a manageable centre.
2. Look Away — Without looking away, name five simultaneous peripheral details—colour, distance, movement, light, geometry.
3. Let Central — Let central and surrounding information coexist until the scene feels larger than the alarm.
win: ✓ The threat stayed visible without swallowing the whole scene.
supports:
• One exhale after “Let Central”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Look Away”.
• “Look Away” proves one signal leads.
• “Hold Trigger” → “Let Central”: what changed?
• I can use “Look Away” amid noise.
formula_flow: Hold Trigger → Look Away → Let Central
safety:
PAUSE
Do not keep a dangerous cue in view when withdrawal is the safer action.

title: PIN A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: A distraction should cost one return address, not a full reconstruction.
steps:
1. Name Object — Name the exact OBJECT currently carrying the task: document, pan, form, email, shelf, or tool.
2. Place — Notice the precise LOCATION inside it: paragraph three, top-left field, second burner, or blue tab.
3. Choose Verb — Choose one NEXT VERB for that location: compare, type, turn, check, send, or place.
4. Reenter — After the interruption, say the three-part address once and act on the verb without rescanning the entire task.

supports:

• “Choose Verb” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Reenter”: what changed from “Name Object”?
• I can use “Place” before autopilot.

title: POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW
goal: Past helplessness should not inherit present equipment.
steps:
1. Imagine Two Sides — Imagine two sides.
2. Then — On the first side, picture your age, knowledge, money, power, support, and choices then.
3. Picture Today — On the second side, picture the same things today.
4. Find The Change — Notice what gives you more choice now.
5. Use One Resource — Pick one resource you have today and use it in one small action.
win: ✓ The past kept its history; today’s resources entered the scene.
supports:
• Exhale after “Use One Resource”; end the lap.
• Re-entry move: “Picture Today”.
• “Find The Change” proves loops can stop.
• Before/after: “Imagine Two Sides” → “Use One Resource”.
• I can use “Then” without another lap.

title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
goal: The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.
steps:
1. Adopt — Take a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety.
2. Refuse Prophecy — Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
3. Hold for Evidence — Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.
win: ✓ Posture held steady while prophecy waited outside.
supports:
• Exhale after “Hold for Evidence”; then keep moving.
• Loop back? Use “Refuse Prophecy”.
• “Refuse Prophecy” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Adopt” → “Hold for Evidence”?
• I can use “Refuse Prophecy” before motivation.
formula_flow: Adopt → Hold the Posture

display.goal: The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.
display.steps:

2. Refuse Prophecy — Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
3. Hold for Evidence — Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.

title: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL
goal: Trembling is movement, not automatic evidence of collapse.
steps:
1. Medically — If medically safe and oriented, permit a small tremor rather than clamping it down.
2. Track Location — Track its location, rhythm, and whether choice remains intact.
3. Let Migrate — Let it stop, continue, or migrate without exaggeration.
4. Let Shake Finish — Ground when the movement ends.
win: ✓ The shake stayed small enough to finish being a shake.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Shake Finish”; no breath-holding.
• On return, repeat “Let Migrate”.
• “Let Migrate” — alarm isn’t command.
• Keep one lesson: “Medically” → “Let Shake Finish”.
• I can use “Track Location” while alarm rises.

title: THREE TEMPERATURE FACTS
goal: Imagined danger must coexist with actual thermal evidence.
steps:
1. Check Temperature — Check temperature at three locations: hands, face, and where clothing meets skin.
2. Use Comparative — Use comparative language—cooler, warmer, neutral—rather than guessing degrees.
3. Let Readings — Let the three readings define the body’s current climate.
win: ✓ The body’s current climate replaced the imagined forecast.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Readings”; notice the room.
• If it flares, choose “Use Comparative”.
• “Use Comparative” proves the present returned.
• “Check Temperature” → “Let Readings”: what changed?
• I can use “Use Comparative” to return here.
formula_flow: Check Temperature → Use Comparative → Let Readings

title: SCENT THE RETURN

title: THREE RINGS OF AGENCY
goal: Do not spend control effort in the observation ring.
steps:
1. Imagine Three Rings — Imagine three rings: CONTROL, INFLUENCE, WATCH.
2. Place Each Part — Put each piece of the problem in the right ring in your mind.
3. Take Action — Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch.
win: ✓ I acted in one ring, asked in one ring, and stopped fighting the third.
supports:
• Exhale after “Take Action”; leave it unanswered.
• On return, repeat “Place Each Part”.
• “Place Each Part” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Difference check: “Imagine Three Rings” → “Take Action”.
• I can use “Place Each Part” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Imagine Three Rings → Place Each Part → Take Action

win: ✓ Experience arrived first. Ownership arrived second.

• Re-entry move: “Catch Ownership”.
• “Wait Sensation” proves thought is observable.
• “Wait Sensation” → “Catch Ownership”: what changed?
• I can use “Catch Ownership” without obeying thought.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps:
1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
win: ✓ The emotional stack revealed which block was actually carrying the weight.
supports:
• Exhale after “Rebuild Stack”; mark the pause.
• Shortcut: “Check Remainder”, once.
• “Check Remainder” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Name Stack” → “Rebuild Stack”?
• I can use “Pull One” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
goal: The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.
steps:
1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.
win: ✓ The compass still works even when the landscape hurts.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Best”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Cost”.
• “Cost” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Keep Best”: what changed from “Identify Critical”?
• I can use “Create Endings” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Identify Critical → Create Endings → Cost → Keep Best
safety:

title: COMMON IS NOT THE SAME AS RIGHT
goal: Frequency cannot settle an ethical question.
steps:
1. State Social — State the social norm and your chosen criteria—harm, fairness, consent, dignity, responsibility.
2. Evaluate — Check the norm against each criterion without citing popularity.
3. Keep Modify — Keep, modify, or reject it based on the ethical comparison.
win: ✓ Popularity lost the argument the moment ethics entered the room.
supports:

• Loop back? Use “Evaluate”.
• “Evaluate” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Before/after: “State Social” → “Keep Modify”.
• I can use “Evaluate” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: State Social → Evaluate → Keep Modify

title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.
steps:
1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source.
win: ✓ The repair stayed mine. The inherited shame went home.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Repair”; release extra blame.
• Re-entry move: “Ask Whether”.
• “Ask Whether” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Identify Whose” → “Keep Repair”: what changed?
• I can use “Ask Whether” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Identify Whose → Ask Whether → Keep Repair

content:
TITLE
RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS

GOAL
A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.

RITUAL
1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source.

WIN
✓ The repair stayed mine. The inherited shame went home.

• Exhale after “Keep Repair”; release extra blame.
• Re-entry move: “Ask Whether”.
• “Ask Whether” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Identify Whose” → “Keep Repair”: what changed?
• I can use “Ask Whether” without owning everything.

FORMULA FLOW
Identify Whose → Ask Whether → Keep Repair

PAUSE
Seek support when shame is severe, trauma-linked, or tied to self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
